title: Join Employees with Department Names
description_markdown: Match each employee with their department name using an INNER JOIN. Return `e.first_name`, `e.last_name`, and `d.dept_name`. Order by `e.emp_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- INNER JOIN employees and departments
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, d.dept_name
FROM employees e
JOIN departments d ON ...
solution_query: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, d.dept_name FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id ORDER BY e.emp_id ASC;
solution_explanation: INNER JOIN selects rows that have matching values in both tables (`e.dept_id = d.dept_id`).
hints: Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.
Query: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, d.dept_name FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id ORDER BY e.emp_id ASC;

title: Retrieve Products with Category Labels
description_markdown: Join `products` with `categories` on `category_id`. Return `p.product_name`, `c.category_name`, and `p.price`. Order by `p.price` descending, then `p.product_id`.
starter_query:
-- Join products and categories
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT p.product_name, c.category_name, p.price FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id ORDER BY p.price DESC, p.product_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Retrieves catalog products enriched with category metadata.
hints: Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.
Query: SELECT p.product_name, c.category_name, p.price FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id ORDER BY p.price DESC, p.product_id ASC;

title: Enumerate Courses Taught by Full Professors
description_markdown: Join `courses` and `professors` on `professor_id`. Filter for professors whose title is 'Full Professor'. Return `c.course_code`, `c.course_name`, and `p.last_name AS professor_last_name`. Order by `c.course_code` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Join courses and professors with filter
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT c.course_code, c.course_name, p.last_name AS professor_last_name FROM courses c JOIN professors p ON c.professor_id = p.professor_id WHERE p.title = 'Full Professor' ORDER BY c.course_code ASC;
solution_explanation: Combines an INNER JOIN with a selective WHERE predicate on faculty title.
hints: Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT c.course_code, c.course_name, p.last_name AS professor_last_name FROM courses c JOIN professors p ON c.professor_id = p.professor_id WHERE p.title = 'Full Professor' ORDER BY c.course_code ASC;

title: Link Customers to Their Placed Orders
description_markdown: Join `customers` with `orders` on `customer_id`. Return `c.customer_id`, `c.first_name`, `o.order_id`, and `o.total_amount`. Order results by `o.order_id` in ascending order.
starter_query:
-- Inner join customers and orders
SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, o.order_id, o.total_amount
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON ...
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, o.order_id, o.total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id ORDER BY o.order_id ASC;
solution_explanation: An INNER JOIN matches records between customers and orders using `c.customer_id = o.customer_id`. Customers who have never placed an order are excluded.
common_mistakes: Omitting table qualifiers leading to ambiguous column errors on customer_id.
interview_tip: Always qualify columns that exist in more than one table to prevent runtime ambiguity errors.
hints: Use `FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id`.
Select the required columns using table aliases.
Query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, o.order_id, o.total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id ORDER BY o.order_id ASC;

title: Match Employees with Project Assignments
description_markdown: Join `employees` with `assignments` on `emp_id`. Return `e.emp_id`, `e.first_name`, `e.last_name`, `a.project_id`, and `a.role`. Order by `e.emp_id` ascending, then `a.project_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Join employees and assignments
SELECT ...
FROM employees e
JOIN assignments a ON ...
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, a.project_id, a.role FROM employees e JOIN assignments a ON e.emp_id = a.emp_id ORDER BY e.emp_id ASC, a.project_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Inner joining `employees` with `assignments` on `e.emp_id = a.emp_id` returns each active role assigned to an employee.
common_mistakes: Using LEFT JOIN when the problem asks for matching assignment records.
interview_tip: When querying many-to-many junction tables, start from the entity table and join the junction table on the primary key.
hints: Order by both `e.emp_id ASC` and `a.project_id ASC`.
Query: SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, a.project_id, a.role FROM employees e JOIN assignments a ON e.emp_id = a.emp_id ORDER BY e.emp_id ASC, a.project_id ASC;

title: Display Student Course Enrollments and Semesters
description_markdown: Join `students` with `enrollments` on `student_id`. Return `s.student_id`, `s.first_name`, `e.course_id`, and `e.semester`. Order results by `s.student_id` ascending, then `e.course_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Join students with enrollments
SELECT ...
FROM students s
JOIN enrollments e ON ...
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT s.student_id, s.first_name, e.course_id, e.semester FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id ORDER BY s.student_id ASC, e.course_id ASC;
solution_explanation: The query combines student demographic info with their semester enrollment roster on matching student_id keys.
common_mistakes: Leaving out table aliases when selecting columns.
interview_tip: Always use meaningful short aliases like s for students and e for enrollments.
hints: Query: SELECT s.student_id, s.first_name, e.course_id, e.semester FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id ORDER BY s.student_id ASC, e.course_id ASC;

title: Filter Line Items with Significant Quantity
description_markdown: Join `order_items` with `products` on `product_id`. Filter for line items where `oi.quantity >= 2`. Return `oi.order_id`, `p.product_name`, `oi.quantity`, and `oi.unit_price`. Order by `oi.order_id` ascending, then `p.product_name` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Join order_items and products with quantity filter
SELECT oi.order_id, p.product_name, oi.quantity, oi.unit_price
FROM order_items oi
JOIN products p ON ...
WHERE ...
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT oi.order_id, p.product_name, oi.quantity, oi.unit_price FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE oi.quantity >= 2 ORDER BY oi.order_id ASC, p.product_name ASC;
solution_explanation: Combines order items and catalog products on product_id while filtering for orders containing multiple units.
common_mistakes: Placing the filter in HAVING without a GROUP BY instead of WHERE.
interview_tip: Row-level filters belong in the WHERE clause, not HAVING.
hints: Query: SELECT oi.order_id, p.product_name, oi.quantity, oi.unit_price FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE oi.quantity >= 2 ORDER BY oi.order_id ASC, p.product_name ASC;

title: Identify Major Departmental Initiatives
description_markdown: Join `departments` and `projects` on `dept_id`. Filter for projects with a `budget >= 400000`. Return `d.dept_name`, `p.project_name`, and `p.budget`. Order by `p.budget` descending, then `d.dept_name` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Join departments and projects
SELECT d.dept_name, p.project_name, p.budget
FROM departments d
JOIN projects p ON ...
WHERE ...
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT d.dept_name, p.project_name, p.budget FROM departments d JOIN projects p ON d.dept_id = p.dept_id WHERE p.budget >= 400000 ORDER BY p.budget DESC, d.dept_name ASC;
solution_explanation: An INNER JOIN filters out departments with no assigned projects and restricts the result to high-budget ventures.
common_mistakes: Confusing department budget with project budget.
interview_tip: Ensure column references use the correct table alias when both tables have a identically named column (like budget).
hints: Query: SELECT d.dept_name, p.project_name, p.budget FROM departments d JOIN projects p ON d.dept_id = p.dept_id WHERE p.budget >= 400000 ORDER BY p.budget DESC, d.dept_name ASC;

title: Find Faculty Teaching Heavy-Credit Courses
description_markdown: Join `professors` with `courses` on `professor_id`. Filter for courses where `credits >= 4`. Return `p.first_name`, `p.last_name`, `c.course_name`, and `c.credits`. Order by `p.last_name` ascending, then `c.course_name` ascending.

-- Join professors and courses
SELECT ...

solution_explanation: Filters the professor and course join to intensive 4-credit offerings.
common_mistakes: Joining on department instead of primary/foreign key professor_id.
interview_tip: Always join on primary and foreign keys rather than text attributes to ensure referential accuracy.
hints: Query: SELECT p.first_name, p.last_name, c.course_name, c.credits FROM professors p JOIN courses c ON p.professor_id = c.professor_id WHERE c.credits >= 4 ORDER BY p.last_name ASC, c.course_name ASC;

title: List Engineering Department Employees
description_markdown: Join `employees` and `departments` on `dept_id`. Filter for members of the 'Engineering' department. Return `e.emp_id`, `e.first_name`, and `e.salary`. Order by `e.salary` descending, then `e.emp_id` ascending.

solution_explanation: Links engineering employees with their department record and sorts them by top compensation.

title: Inspect High-Scoring Course Assessments
description_markdown: Join `enrollments` and `marks` on `enrollment_id`. Filter for assessment scores where `score >= 90`. Return `e.student_id`, `e.course_id`, `m.assessment_type`, and `m.score`. Order by `m.score` descending, then `e.student_id` ascending.

solution_explanation: Returns individual student academic assessment records where the student earned honors grades (>= 90).

hints: Query: SELECT e.student_id, e.course_id, m.assessment_type, m.score FROM enrollments e JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id WHERE m.score >= 90 ORDER BY m.score DESC, e.student_id ASC;

title: Retrieve Orders Exceeding 500 Dollars
description_markdown: Join `customers` with `orders` on `customer_id`. Filter for orders where `total_amount >= 500`. Return `c.email`, `o.order_id`, and `o.total_amount`. Order by `o.total_amount` descending, then `o.order_id` ascending.

common_mistakes: Filtering using customer_id instead of total_amount.

hints: Query: SELECT c.email, o.order_id, o.total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.total_amount >= 500 ORDER BY o.total_amount DESC, o.order_id ASC;

title: Inspect Top-Rated Project Contributors
description_markdown: Join `projects` and `assignments` on `project_id`. Filter for assignments with `rating >= 4.5`. Return `p.project_name`, `a.emp_id`, `a.hours_worked`, and `a.rating`. Order by `a.rating` descending, then `p.project_name` ascending, then `a.emp_id` ascending.

title: Connect Review Authors with Feedback

title: Trace Historic Employee Compensation Changes
description_markdown: Join `employees` and `salaries_history` on `emp_id`. Return `e.first_name`, `e.last_name`, `sh.effective_date`, and `sh.salary AS historical_salary`. Order by `e.last_name` ascending, then `sh.effective_date` ascending.

SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, sh.effective_date, sh.salary AS historical_salary
FROM employees e

solution_query: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, sh.effective_date, sh.salary AS historical_salary FROM employees e JOIN salaries_history sh ON e.emp_id = sh.emp_id ORDER BY e.last_name ASC, sh.effective_date ASC;

common_mistakes: Selecting e.salary instead of sh.salary.
interview_tip: Audit logs require carefully separating the current state in the primary table from historical values in the ledger table.
hints: Query: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, sh.effective_date, sh.salary AS historical_salary FROM employees e JOIN salaries_history sh ON e.emp_id = sh.emp_id ORDER BY e.last_name ASC, sh.effective_date ASC;

title: Catalog Premium Products by Category

solution_query: SELECT p.product_name, c.category_name, p.price FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id WHERE p.price > 100 ORDER BY p.price DESC, p.product_name ASC;

title: Aggregate Department Headcounts via Inner Join
description_markdown: Join `departments` and `employees` on `dept_id`. Group by `d.dept_id` and `d.dept_name`. Return `d.dept_name` and `COUNT(e.emp_id) AS employee_count`. Order by `employee_count` descending, then `d.dept_name` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Join and group by department
SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS employee_count
FROM departments d
JOIN employees e ON ...
GROUP BY ...
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS employee_count FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.dept_name ORDER BY employee_count DESC, d.dept_name ASC;
solution_explanation: Counts active employees per department. Departments without any employees are automatically excluded by the INNER JOIN.
common_mistakes: Leaving d.dept_name out of the GROUP BY clause.
interview_tip: In ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY mode, any unaggregated column in SELECT must be included in GROUP BY.
hints: Query: SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS employee_count FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.dept_name ORDER BY employee_count DESC, d.dept_name ASC;

title: Calculate Total Customer Spend on Completed Orders
description_markdown: Join `customers` and `orders` on `customer_id`. Filter where `o.order_status = 'completed'`. Group by `c.customer_id` and `c.first_name`. Return `c.first_name` and `SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent`. Order by `total_spent` descending, then `c.first_name` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Join customers and completed orders
SELECT c.first_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON ...
WHERE ...
GROUP BY ...
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT c.first_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name ORDER BY total_spent DESC, c.first_name ASC;
solution_explanation: Calculates lifetime completed order value per customer by joining the tables and filtering prior to aggregation.
common_mistakes: Including refunded or cancelled orders in the sum.
interview_tip: Filtering before grouping in the WHERE clause reduces the rows fed to the aggregation engine.
hints: Query: SELECT c.first_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name ORDER BY total_spent DESC, c.first_name ASC;

title: Calculate Teaching Load per Faculty Member
description_markdown: Join `professors` with `courses` on `professor_id`. Group by `p.professor_id`, `p.last_name`, and `p.department`. Return `p.last_name`, `p.department`, and `COUNT(c.course_id) AS courses_taught`. Order by `courses_taught` descending, then `p.last_name` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Join professors and courses
SELECT p.last_name, p.department, COUNT(c.course_id) AS courses_taught
FROM professors p
JOIN courses c ON ...
GROUP BY ...
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT p.last_name, p.department, COUNT(c.course_id) AS courses_taught FROM professors p JOIN courses c ON p.professor_id = c.professor_id GROUP BY p.professor_id, p.last_name, p.department ORDER BY courses_taught DESC, p.last_name ASC;
solution_explanation: Aggregates course count per teaching professor, excluding unassigned faculty members.
common_mistakes: Missing p.department from the GROUP BY clause.
interview_tip: Group by the primary key plus all non-aggregated display columns to maintain strict SQL compatibility.
hints: Query: SELECT p.last_name, p.department, COUNT(c.course_id) AS courses_taught FROM professors p JOIN courses c ON p.professor_id = c.professor_id GROUP BY p.professor_id, p.last_name, p.department ORDER BY courses_taught DESC, p.last_name ASC;

title: Determine Average Product Price by Category
description_markdown: Join `categories` with `products` on `category_id`. Group by `c.category_id` and `c.category_name`. Return `c.category_name` and `ROUND(AVG(p.price), 2) AS avg_price`. Order by `avg_price` descending, then `c.category_name` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Join categories and products
SELECT c.category_name, ROUND(AVG(p.price), 2) AS avg_price
FROM categories c
JOIN products p ON ...
GROUP BY ...
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT c.category_name, ROUND(AVG(p.price), 2) AS avg_price FROM categories c JOIN products p ON c.category_id = p.category_id GROUP BY c.category_id, c.category_name ORDER BY avg_price DESC, c.category_name ASC;
solution_explanation: Computes the mean catalog price for each merchandise category.
common_mistakes: Forgetting ROUND(..., 2).
interview_tip: Rounding averages to two decimals is standard financial formatting in reporting queries.
hints: Query: SELECT c.category_name, ROUND(AVG(p.price), 2) AS avg_price FROM categories c JOIN products p ON c.category_id = p.category_id GROUP BY c.category_id, c.category_name ORDER BY avg_price DESC, c.category_name ASC;

title: Calculate Total Work Hours Committed per Project
description_markdown: Join `projects` and `assignments` on `project_id`. Group by `p.project_id` and `p.project_name`. Return `p.project_name` and `SUM(a.hours_worked) AS total_hours`. Order by `total_hours` descending, then `p.project_name` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Join projects and assignments to sum hours
SELECT p.project_name, SUM(a.hours_worked) AS total_hours
FROM projects p
JOIN assignments a ON ...
GROUP BY ...
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT p.project_name, SUM(a.hours_worked) AS total_hours FROM projects p JOIN assignments a ON p.project_id = a.project_id GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name ORDER BY total_hours DESC, p.project_name ASC;
solution_explanation: Sums all logged assignment hours per project to measure effort expenditure.

Group by `c.course_id` and `c.course_name`. Return `c.course_name` and `ROUND(AVG(m.score), 2) AS avg_final_score`. Order by `avg_final_score` descending, then `c.course_name` ascending.
starter_query:

FROM courses c
JOIN enrollments e ON ...
JOIN marks m ON ...

solution_query: SELECT c.course_name, ROUND(AVG(m.score), 2) AS avg_final_score FROM courses c JOIN enrollments e ON c.course_id = e.course_id JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id WHERE m.assessment_type = 'final' GROUP BY c.course_id, c.course_name ORDER BY avg_final_score DESC, c.course_name ASC;

Filter with `HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 2`. Return `c.first_name`, `c.last_name`, and `COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders_count`. Order by `completed_orders_count` descending, then `c.last_name` ascending.
starter_query:

JOIN orders o ON ...
WHERE ...
GROUP BY ...
HAVING ...
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 2 ORDER BY completed_orders_count DESC, c.last_name ASC;
